questions.question: **In the following question, four words are given out of which one word is correctly spelt. Select the correctly spelt word.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Impoverish__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The correctly spelt word is '**impoverish**' which means '**make (a person or area) poor**'.
 
• **Example: **Poor farming practices impoverished the soil.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Synonyms of Impoverish: **pauperize, reduce, wipe out
 
• **Antonyms of Impoverish: **enrich, richen

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

So he decided he

A - people, hopefully, none

B - better place with fewer

C - would go far away, to a
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__CBA__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

C is the first part as it states what the person decided.

B follows C as it states where he wanted to go.

A completes the sentence. Option 1 is thus the correct answer.

**Thus the sentence becomes: **So he decided he would go far away, to a better place with fewer people, hopefully, none.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

Humongous changes (has occurred) in the last two decades.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Have occurred__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• The subject and the verb must agree with each other in a sentence.
 
• Here the **subject** 'Humongous changes' **is plural**, so **plural verb** should be used after it.
 
• The present perfect tense refers to an action or state that either occurred at an indefinite time in the past (e.g., we have talked before) or began in the past and continued to the present time (e.g., he has grown impatient over the last hour). This tense is formed by have/has + the past participle.

**Thus the correct sentence is: ***Humongous changes **have occurred** in the last two decades.*

• **when **is used to refer **at what time; at the time at which**
 
• **which **is used to refer back to an idea or situation expressed in a previous sentence or sentences, especially when you want to give your opinion about it.
 
• **While **is used to refer during the time that, or at the same time as
 
• **who **is used as the subject or object of a verb to show which person you are referring to, or to add information about a person just mentioned. It is used for people, not things

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

Why did your mother write such a book?

options.text: Why was such a book written by your mother?
Why is such a book written by your mother?
Why your mother wrote such a book?
Why was such a book wrote by your mother?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Why was such a book written by your mother?**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• The following rule should be followed while changing the voice of an 'assertive sentence' in the simple past tense.

 
 
• subject + V2 + object (Active)
 
• object + was/were + V3 + by + subject (Passive)
 
• For interrogative sentence 'did + V₁' changes to 'was/were + V₃'
 
 
 
• ​Example: The school management organised the annual function. (Active)

The annual function was organised by the school management. (Passive)

 
• **'such a book' **becomes the subject and **'your mother' **becomes the object.
 
• **'by' **is used before the object.
 
• The final sentence- *Why was such a book written by your mother?*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which best expresses the meaning of the given word.**

Allay
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Relieve__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **Meaning of the words given are:**

 
 
• The word '**allay**' means '**diminish or put at rest (fear, suspicion, or worry)**.'

 **Example: **The government is trying to allay public fears/concern about the spread of the disease.
 
• **Relieve **means to make an unpleasant feeling, such as pain or worry, less strong

 **Example: **She relieved her boredom at home by learning how to type
 
• **Understand **means to know the meaning of something that someone says

 **Example:** She explained the whole idea again, but I still didn't understand.
 
• **Increase **means to (make something) become larger in amount or size

 **Example: ***I*ncidents of armed robbery have increased over the last few years.
 
• **Annoy: **to make someone angry

 **Example: **Tina really annoyed me in the meeting this morning.
 
 
 
• Thus 'relieve' is the correct answer.

• **The meanings of the words are:**

 
 
• **Grudging:** unwilling; disinclined

 **Example: **She won the grudging respect of her boss.
 
• **Envious:** jealous; disinclined

 **Example: **I'm very envious of your new coat - it's beautiful.
 
• **Favoring:** supporting

 **Example: **These are the running shoes favoured by marathon runners.
 
• **Generous: **kind

 **Example: **It was generous of you to lend me the money.
 
• **Contented:** to say that something is true or is a fact

 **Example: **The lawyer contended (that) her client had never been near the scene of the crime.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **envious**

 **Example: **Hundreds of dissidents are seeking refuge/asylum in the US embassy.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

The long-term capital gains on listed securities (1)/and the dividend tax on equity mutual funds are the right steps (2)/to generate resources required for drive demand in rural India. (3)/No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__3__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• The error lies in part 3 of the sentence as the verb '**drive**' in **transitive** form is incorrect here and the correct form of the verb **must be in 'ing' form 'driving'** as 'for' is mentioned in the sentence.
 
• Prepositions are followed by a noun or a pronoun as an object of preposition.
 
• A gerund is a verb form that acts as a noun, so 'driving' is the correct word to be used here.

**Thus, the correct sentence is: ***The long-term capital gains on listed securities and the dividend tax on equity mutual funds are the right steps to generate resources required for **driving demand** in rural India.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

I seen (1)/that it (2)/is getting dark. (3)/No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__1__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **'see' **should be there in place of **'seen'**
 
• We use the **simple** **present tense** when an action is happening right now
 
• The error lies in part 1 of the sentence as the verb 'seen' is incorrect and must be in simple present 'see' to make the sentence correct. The whole sentence is in simple present tense.

**Thus, the correct sentence is: ***I **see **that it is getting dark*
